subject.title: [Bug]: Rapid multi-part Telegram turns fragment into parallel child sessions instead of one batched turn

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a shared, opt-in inbound-message coalescing capability for chat channels, beginning with Telegram, rather than preserving immediate dispatch for every distinct inbound message?
rationale: The requested behavior adds latency and a new configuration/policy surface across routing, sessions, media, commands, and transcript semantics; source and documentation show no existing contract that determines those tradeoffs.

options.title: Sponsor a shared opt-in coalescer
options.body: Add one gateway-owned, session-and-sender-scoped batching policy with conservative defaults and Telegram as the first consumer.

options.title: Keep immediate dispatch
options.body: Retain the current per-message dispatch contract and treat multi-message conversational pacing as a user or prompt-level workflow rather than runtime behavior.

options.title: Request a narrower design proposal
options.body: Keep this issue open for a bounded design covering commands, media, group senders, session resets, and upgrade behavior before committing to implementation.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a shared opt-in coalescer
recommendation.body: Add one gateway-owned, session-and-sender-scoped batching policy with conservative defaults and Telegram as the first consumer.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin/channel boundary work and the repository vision make this the strongest available product and architecture routing candidate.
